gap: No result ChatGPT got prices the whole GL.iNet travel line on one dated day. On 2026-11-08 the GL.iNet US store lists the Slate 7 at $159.99, $30 more than the $129.99 Beryl 7, and lists the Slate 7 Pro in stock at $239.99. Stayingconnectedabroad says the Slate 7 Pro is not yet available in the US, and itechguides and pointscapitaltravel both give the Slate 7 as $169.99.
standout_why: I compared stayingconnectedabroad.com (2026-10-12), itechguides.com (2026-08-11) and pointscapitaltravel.com (2026-10-18). Stayingconnectedabroad gives only rounded, undated prices ('about $99', 'about $130', 'about $150 to $160') and says the Slate 7 Pro is not available in the US, which the US store shows is wrong today. Itechguides has exact prices observed 2026-08-10, with a Slate 7 price ($169.99) and VPN figure (540/100 Mbps) that no longer match. Pointscapitaltravel prices only the Beryl AX, Slate 7 ($169.99 sale), UTR and UTR-LR. None of the three prices the Slate AX ($119.99) or Slate 7 Pro ($239.99), and none mentions the ASUS RT-BE58 Go. However, itechguides already prints the Beryl 7 and Beryl AX prices next to their maker WireGuard figures, so a reader can work out the cost per Mbps from a rival page. That is why this scores 1, not 2.
decides: It backs the Beryl 7 as the pick. At GL.iNet US prices today, the Beryl 7 costs $31 more than the Beryl AX for 3.7× the maker-rated WireGuard speed ($0.118 per Mbps vs $0.33). It costs $30 less than the Slate 7 for 2.2× the WireGuard speed. This weakens ChatGPT's 'best value' label on the Beryl AX, unless the shopper's hotel connection is under about 300 Mbps anyway. Pointscapitaltravel says hotel Wi-Fi is usually the bottleneck. The Slate 7 only wins if the shopper pays for the touchscreen.
